lesson_title: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16... Then 31. Why Fitting Is Not Proving
hook_text: Dots on a circle, join them all, count the pieces: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Everyone says 32. Everyone is wrong.
clip_script: Put dots on a circle and join every pair. Count the regions. One dot, 1. Two, 2. Three, 4. Four, 8. Five, 16. Doubling — so six dots gives 32? Draw it. Count carefully. Thirty-one. Five terms that fit proved nothing; one term that fails proves everything. So how do you KNOW a rule? Explain it from the picture. Square tables in a row seat 4, 6, 8. Rule 2n plus 2 — and here is the why: n people along the top, n along the bottom, one at each end. Every piece of the rule points at a piece of the picture. That is a justification. "It works for the first three" is only a check. Finish the sentence: this works because...
visual_style: A circle gains dots one at a time with chords drawn between every pair and a region counter ticking 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 then stuttering to 31; cut to a row of square tables with stick figures counted along top, bottom and ends.
mood: Dramatic reveal, then calm and clear.
pacing: Rising rhythm to the 32 trap, a hard stop at 31, then steady explanation.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to defend every rule you write.
